title: t5: count of tokens in the same class as the last token (mlp0 -> head 1.0 -> mlp1)
label: verified
behavior: Input BOS + 5 tokens from {gi, ke, ki, me, su}; at the last position the model outputs one digit token '0'..'5'.
summary: All numbers are from the local-full backend (full precision). The model outputs how many of the 5 input tokens (the last one included) belong to the same class as the last token, where the classes are {ke, ki}, {gi, me} and {su}. Three components implement it: mlp0 prepares a per-token feature at every token position, head 1.0 at the last position attends evenly to BOS and to every same-class position (so the BOS share is 1/(count+1)), and mlp1 at the last position turns that into the digit. Heads 0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 1.1 and 1.2 play no part. The algorithm matches the model on 300/300 held-out inputs and the circuit passes necessity, sufficiency and null controls.
pseudocode:
cls = {ke:'k', ki:'k', gi:'g', me:'g', su:'s'}
# mlp0 (positions 1-5): per-token class feature
# head 1.0 (query = last pos): uniform attention over BOS + positions with cls == cls[last]  -> BOS share = 1/(count+1)
# mlp1 (last pos): decode share -> digit
count = sum(cls[x] == cls[x5] for x in x1..x5)
output = digit(count)   # token id 7 + count

claims.text: The model reproduces its recorded outputs exactly (accuracy 1.0, n=200).
Function: output = number of input tokens in the same class as the last token, classes {ke,ki},{gi,me},{su}; predict() agrees with the model on 300/300 held-out inputs.

The circuit is mlp0, head 1.0 and mlp1: jointly mean-ablated the metric falls to 0.023 of clean; individually 1.0 -> -0.03, mlp0 -> 0.0, mlp1 -> -0.0004. On held-out data ablating the circuit gives -0.006 of clean (accuracy 0.30) while ablating everything else leaves 1.0.
Heads 0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 1.1 and 1.2 play no part: jointly mean-ablating all five leaves 1.0 of clean, and patching layer-0 attention output has zero effect at every position.

Head 1.0 at the last position splits attention exactly evenly between BOS and same-class positions, including a different symbol of the same class (1/3, 1/3, 0, 0, 0, 1/3 on count-2 prompts), so the BOS share encodes 1/(count+1).
mlp0 acts at every token position 1-5 (denoising effect 0.27-0.36 per position, 0 at BOS); mlp1 acts only at the last position (effect 1.0 there, 0 elsewhere).
Layer-1 attention output at the last position is all mlp1 needs: patching it alone restores the full metric.

nodes.label: head 1.0: even attention over BOS + same-class positions

edges.label: class feature (query at last pos, keys at pos 1-5)

limitations: The mlp0 -> head 1.0 edge is inferred from mlp0's necessity at positions 1-5 plus the class-matched attention pattern; it was not path-patched (path_patching only takes heads as senders), so whether mlp0 feeds the query, the key or both is not measured.
What mlp0 writes was not decoded (no probe run); 'class feature' is the simplest reading consistent with E0008 and E0012.
The class table was inferred from examples and confirmed by 300/300 agreement and the E0008 prompts, not by exhaustive enumeration of all 3125 inputs.
The metric saturates at +/-1, so effect sizes are close to accuracy-like and do not resolve small partial contributions.
open_questions: Does mlp0 feed head 1.0 through the query, the key, or both?
How do mlp1's neurons map the fractions 1/2..1/6 to the five digits?
